title: Ibrahim tested
hookLine: Ibrahim is tested with commands, fulfills them, and is made a leader for people (2:124)

lines: NOT THE HARDEST OPERATION ON DAY ONE.
cards: Nobody hands a new surgeon the hardest operation on day one. First the exams, then years of watching, then small procedures with someone standing behind them. Trust comes after testing.

Al-Baqarah has spent pages remembering a people's gifts and stumbles. Now, at verse one hundred twenty-four, it turns to a man honored as a father in faith by Jews, Christians and Muslims, and starts with a test.

teach.h: TESTED WITH WORDS, AND FULFILLED THEM
teach.b: His Lord tested Ibrahim with certain words, commands, and he fulfilled them. Then God says, in Pickthall's words: “Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind.”
The word for leader is imam: the one in front, the same word for whoever leads a prayer. What were the commands? The verse doesn't say.
Ibn Abbas, in one report, says practices of purity and the rites of pilgrimage.
Others point to the great trials of Ibrahim's life: the fire he was thrown into, leaving his wife and son in a barren valley, the dream of sacrificing his son. The Qur'an leaves the list open.
What it keeps is the order: tested, fulfilled, then trusted. Then Ibrahim does a very human thing.
Just made a leader, his first words are: and from my descendants? God's answer: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers. Leadership isn't an inheritance; each generation is tested for itself.
Muslims read this verse in different ways. Sunni scholars generally take imam here to mean a model of faith for all people.
For Shia Muslims it's a foundational verse for the imamate, a rank of divinely chosen leadership given after testing, kept from wrongdoers. Both hear the same order in it.
Look back at this week: a fire lit and lost, a gnat, Adam returning, a favor remembered, a cow, a stone.

teach.h: THIS WEEK: GIVEN MUCH, AND TESTED
teach.b: People given much and tested, Muslims included, as the teachers read it.

how: Muslims honor Ibrahim as a model of faith through trial; Sunni scholars read imam in 2:124 as a leader in faith for all people, while Shia Muslims read the verse as foundational for the imamate.

o: tested only once, by the order to sacrifice his son
tried with unnamed commands, fulfilled them, then made imam
tested by his descendants, who inherited his leadership

p: the one in front, the leader

s: the Qur'an lists exactly which commands Ibrahim was tested with
it leaves them unnamed; commentators offer several answers.
the word for leader in 2:124 is the same word used for a prayer leader
Sunni and Shia Muslims read 2:124 in exactly the same way
for Shia Muslims it's foundational for the imamate; Sunni scholars generally read a model of faith.

games.q: you're Ibrahim. you've just been told you're a leader for people. what do you say?
games.why: and from my descendants? the answer: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers. leadership isn't inherited; each generation is tested.

practice: Think of one obligation you've been carrying half done, the form, the visit, the apology, the repair, and picture its last step: your own hands doing it, and what it's like on the other side.
Stay there a moment before you open your eyes.

wordCard.voice: Ibrahim tested. Tried with commands the Qur'an leaves unnamed, he fulfilled them, and only then was made an imam, a leader for people. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a leader, the one in front; used for Ibrahim in 2:124 and for whoever leads a prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: tested, then trusted. In Ibrahim's story, the order is what matters. That's the week.
